Comment: A 150-day season from 5 December to early May for a north-facing resort with its base at 1,400 m and its ridge at 1,900 m on the northern side of the Alps. Statistics at the base elevation, in the range of 1991-2020 station normals for 1,400-1,500 m sites in the Bavarian, Tyrolean and Bernese Alps: January means around -6 C, about 12-15 precipitation days a month bringing 80-110 mm of water (roughly 1-1.5 m of snow at 12-15:1), prevailing west-north-west winds of 13-17 km/h with foehn and frontal gusts, cloudy Decembers and sunnier Februarys. The generator interpolates between periods by season day, adds AR(1) daily anomalies (temperature autocorrelation 0.72, wind 0.55) and keeps storms going with 55 percent persistence; forecast error grows 1.4 C, 15 percent precipitation and 6 km/h per day of lead. Snow-to-liquid ratio runs from 8:1 near the snow line to 15:1 in deep cold.

Periods.Label: Early December
Periods.Comment: Opening weeks: short days, frequent frontal snowfalls from the west-north-west, cloudy and humid; the base is thin and every storm counts. 5-23 December.

Periods.Label: Christmas week
Periods.Comment: Christmas to Epiphany: the busiest two weeks and the most variable weather of the winter, with the highest storm frequency and the widest temperature swings (a Christmas thaw or a -20 C night are both normal). 24 December-5 January.

Periods.Label: January cold
Periods.Comment: The coldest part of the winter: January mean around -6.5 C at 1,400 m with inversions in the valley and dry, cold northerly snowfalls; the best snowmaking window of the season. 6-23 January.

Periods.Label: Late January
Periods.Comment: Still deep winter, days lengthening; high-pressure spells with cold clear nights become more common. 24 January-6 February.

Periods.Label: February
Periods.Comment: The sunny month: the driest and least cloudy period, strong daytime warming on south faces already, the deepest base of the year; the school-holiday peak. 7-28 February.

Periods.Label: Early March
Periods.Comment: Spring begins at the base: afternoon melt and night refreeze (a 9 C diurnal range), wetter storms with a rising snow line, and the first foehn days from the south-west. 1-20 March.

Periods.Label: Late March
Periods.Comment: Corn-snow season at the base with rain-on-snow events in the wetter storms; the ridge still gets snow. First convective showers with lightning. 21 March-5 April.

Periods.Label: April
Periods.Comment: Easter skiing: warm, showery afternoons with thunderstorms, the base melting from below; snowmaking is over and grooming means moving what is left. 6-21 April.

Periods.Label: Late April
Periods.Comment: Closing weeks: the base area is grass by the end, only the upper mountain and north faces hold; frequent rain and afternoon storms. 22 April-3 May.
